rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule re-read at current wording (rule-drift target). Walked every pronoun/demonstrative under a sequential read: chunk 0 line 15 'That alone' -> the two-window quote just given (line 11-13); line 17 'the agent's raw power' is the first bare 'agent' in this file but this is an AE101 supplementary deep in the arc (M4->M5 per curriculum.js) and 'agent' is the training's own spine noun (the whole training is Agentic Engineering 101) -- arc-earned carve-out, not a fresh coinage; line 19 'This is the mercury problem' -> the drift description in the immediately preceding sentence; line 23 'this is where Clean Code changes meaning' -> the local-success/global-drift idea two sentences up. Chunk 2 line 47 'the engineer gives it many small, local tripwires' -> 'it' binds to 'the LLM' named earlier in the same sentence. Chunk 4 line 55 'that makes it harder for an agent' -> the mutation-tester action just described. Chunk 5 line 59 'Both expose code that is hard to trust' -> 'CRAP' and 'complexity metrics', both named in the same bolded lead two words earlier; maintainer note at line 109 independently resolves this exact sentence for the adjacent writing-rule tension, and on a fresh read it also confirms 'Both' has two named antecedents in-chunk, not zero. Chunk 6 line 63 'This is classic Clean Code' -> the preceding sentence's claim. Chunk 7 line 67 'it needs instruments' -> 'Architecture', same sentence. Chunk 8 line 83 'It becomes more like active management' -> 'The engineer's job', preceding sentence. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent anywhere in the body; the harm this rule guards (a reader stalled on an unresolvable pointer) is not present.

Every content chunk (1-9) opens with a bolded named-practice lead and carries 3-6 full sentences plus, on all but chunks 3 and 6, an attributed supporting quote. Shortest chunk (4, 'Mutation testing...', lines 53-56) still has three complete sentences building one self-contained claim. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked all nine header/body pairs: 'Unit tests shrink the agent's room to improvise' (45) vs 'the agent has more room to improvise' when tests are thin (47) -- direct match. 'Metrics are the dashboard, not the wheel' (57) vs 'they give the engineer a dashboard' (59) -- match. 'Small units leave fewer places to hide' (61) vs 'fewer escape routes' (63) -- match. 'Architecture needs an instrument panel too' (65) vs 'it needs instruments' (67) -- match. The remaining five headers restate their chunk's own opening bolded-lead sentence directly. No header is contradicted by its chunk's content.

Fresh scans over body lines 1-106: `grep -nE '\. Not [A-Za-z]+\.'` -> 0; `grep -niE 'one of the most|most useful|best way|game-chang|revolution'` -> 0; `grep -niE 'could be (more|less)|roughly|approximately'` -> 0. Two judgment-only candidates checked and cleared: (a) line 77's five-question run ('What is the system? Where are the boundaries? ... What tradeoff is acceptable?') is a rhetorical-question stack, not one of the rule's five named tic shapes (no-Not-X-Y-Z, anaphora triple, self-grading superlative, number+retraction, abstraction-noun stack, empty-leg verb triplet) -- closest candidate, stays inside because it doesn't match any listed pattern and each question adds a distinct axis (system identity, boundaries, invariants, allowed deps, acceptable tradeoff). (b) same line's 'active management of intent, evidence, and structure' reads abstraction-noun-stack-shaped, but the five preceding questions already cashed out the concrete referents (system, boundaries, invariants, dependencies, tradeoffs), so the summary noun-list closes a paragraph that has already done the concrete work rather than substituting for it -- stays inside. The only anaphora-shaped structure in the file is the verbatim attributed quote at lines 85-91 (Assemblers/Compilers/AIs/'Deal with it'): each leg names a genuinely different abstraction rung and the fourth leg pivots to new content (the human's remaining role), so it passes the rule's own carry-new-content test; it is also a sourced quote, so rewriting it to dodge a cadence scan would falsify sourced text rather than fix a defect.
